title: Uniform truncation maps for families under a functor of finite amplitude
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories in a fixed universe [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant class of objects of $\mathcal A$ containing zero and closed under small coproducts. Let $G:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be an exact triangulated functor commuting with integer shifts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose $c\in\mathbf N$, $G(D^{\ge a})\subset D^{\ge a}$ for every integer $a$, and $G(L)\in D^{\le b+c}$ whenever $L\in D^{\le b}$ and every $H^j(L)$ belongs to $\mathcal P$. Bounds use the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For any small family $(K_s)_{s\in I}$ with all $H^j(K_s)\in\mathcal P$, and integer $m$, put
$$U_s=\tau_{\le m}K_s,\quad u_s:U_s\to K_s,\qquad V_s=\tau_{\ge m-c}U_s,\quad v_s:U_s\to V_s,$$
using the canonical good truncation maps [def-kun-truncations]. Then every $V_s$ has $\mathcal P$-cohomology in the common interval $[m-c,m]$, and each of the following four maps is invertible in $\mathcal B$:
$$H^m(G(\bigoplus_su_s)),\quad H^m(G(\bigoplus_sv_s)),\quad H^m(\bigoplus_sG(u_s)),\quad H^m(\bigoplus_sG(v_s)).$$
Here all sums are ambient derived coproducts, and $\bigoplus_su_s$ and $\bigoplus_sv_s$ denote the maps induced by the specified coprojections. The assertions are natural in the family $(K_s)$, include the empty family, and require no common cohomological bound on the $K_s$.

proof.text: Use the Grothendieck AB4 instance (AB5 implies exact coproducts) and its K-injective resolutions. The proved source-library instance DerivedCategory.preservesColimitsOfShape_homologyFunctor identifies cohomology of any coproduct with the coproduct of the cohomologies by the canonical sigmaComparison. The source-library lemmas isLE_sigma and isGE_sigma retain common bounds. Isomorphism invariance of P and hPsum retain P-cohomology. These apply to empty coproducts as well.

Put U_s=truncLE m K_s and V_s=truncGE (m-c) U_s. Use the existing homologyProperty_truncLE and homologyProperty_truncGE lemmas: cohomology is unchanged in the surviving degrees and zero outside. P contains zero, so both families retain P-cohomology. The standard truncation instances give V_s >= m-c and V_s <= m. No extension closure of P is required.

Apply G to the canonical triangle U_s -> K_s -> truncGT m K_s. Its last vertex maps into degrees >= m+1 by hGge. The long exact cohomology sequence, or source-library isIso_homologyMap_mor1, makes H^m(G(u_s)) invertible. Apply G to truncLE (m-c-1) U_s -> U_s -> V_s. Its first vertex retains P-cohomology; hGle puts its image in degrees <= m-1. The long exact sequence, or isIso_homologyMap_mor2, makes H^m(G(v_s)) invertible.

Take coproducts of these actual distinguished triangles, using the proved coproductTriangle_distinguished theorem. Their outer vertices retain the necessary cohomological bounds by step 1. The lower triangle first vertex also retains P-cohomology by steps 1-2. Repeat the previous step after applying G to these coproduct triangles. Their first and second arrows are exactly Sigma.map u and Sigma.map v, respectively. Thus both comparisons with coproduct inside G are invertible, without any truncation-coproduct comparison or arrow-kernel calculation.

The source-library isIso_homologyFunctor_map_sigmaMap, using preservation of coproducts by cohomology, transfers the individual isomorphisms of step 3 to the coproducts of G(u_s) and G(v_s). These are the two comparisons with coproduct after G.

For any transformation f of discrete diagrams, the canonical Sigma.isoColimit isomorphisms satisfy e_X.hom >> colim.map f = Sigma.map (fun i => f.app i) >> e_Y.hom. Check this identity on every coprojection. Apply the relevant functor and cancel the mapped isomorphisms. The proved private helper isIso_map_colimMap_of_sigmaMap performs precisely this transport for all four maps. The whiskered components in the statement are definitionally the resulting colim.map expressions. All arrows remain natural in K; no boundedness of K or nonempty-index assumption has been used.

Step 5: in the long exact segment of the triangle τ≤m→L→τ≥m+1, H^{m-1}(GW)=H^m(GW)=0 by the lower-bound hypothesis. Step 6: G(τ≤a-1 L)∈D^{≤m-1} kills H^m and H^{m+1}, applied to U_s and to ⊕U_s. Step 8 uses only θ in B, with no claim that G commutes with sums. Step 9 covers the empty family. lean.note: Families are Discrete I diagrams. Each comparison is explicitly the component at K of a natural transformation formed by whiskering the canonical truncation arrows, the ambient derived coproduct functor colim, G, and H^m. This expresses naturality without arbitrary maps or extra closure assumptions on P. Object, morphism, localization, and indexing universes are explicit and independent except for the common indexing universe w.
